<question>
Ley 820 de 2003 is said to give eviction cases a preferential procedure decided in a single instance (art. 39). Is that article still in force?
</question>

<answer>
No. Article 39 of Ley 820 de 2003 (Trámite preferente y única instancia) is marked as repealed in the Senate's compilation of the law. [1] The repeal is attributed to subparagraph (c) of article 626 of Ley 1564 de 2012, the Código General del Proceso, with effect from 1 January 2014. [1] The repeal is subject to the transition rule in point 6 of article 627 of that law. [1] The same compilation marks articles 35, 36, 38 and 40 of Ley 820 de 2003 as repealed in the same way. [1] The source does not include Ley 1564 de 2012, so it cannot state which rule applies in place of article 39. [1]
</answer>

<reference>
No. The Senate's compilation of Ley 820 de 2003 marks art. 39 (Trámite preferente y única instancia) as repealed by subparagraph (c) of art. 626 of Ley 1564 de 2012 (the Código General del Proceso), with effect from 1 January 2014 and subject to the transition rule in point 6 of art. 627 of that law. The compilation marks arts. 35, 36, 38 and 40 the same way. The corpus does not include Ley 1564 de 2012, so it cannot say which rule applies instead.
</reference>
